name: CNBTX-A

card.summary: A Chinese-made botulinum toxin type A product, also called Nanfeng toxin, used like other toxins to relax muscles that cause frown lines and soften the upper face.
card.note: Described as not licensed in any country; a 2008 letter reported its potency exceeded labeled units.

quick.overview:
CNBTX-A is a botulinum toxin type A product made in China and sold under the Nanfeng name. Botulinum toxins relax targeted facial muscles, which softens frown lines and brow creases, and it is discussed in hardmaxx circles as a lower-cost option.

Unlike licensed brands such as Botox, it is described in the source note as unlicensed in any country. The one published item identified is a 2008 letter reporting on its potency in a standard test.
quick.how: As with other toxins, it would be injected by a practitioner into specific facial muscles, with effects lasting a few months in general for botulinum toxins. Units differ between brands, which is why products are not interchangeable.
quick.risks: A 2008 Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology letter titled for potency exceeding labeled units points to a unit-labeling concern. Licensed toxins carry brand-specific dosing and the FDA has said brands are not interchangeable. Unlicensed products have no regulator oversight.

lead: CNBTX-A, also called Nanfeng botulinum toxin, is a Chinese-made botulinum toxin type A preparation.[1] People interested in toxin treatments for frown lines and a smoother upper face may come across it as a cheaper alternative to licensed brands.

Botulinum toxin is widely used cosmetically for wrinkles in the upper third of the face, most often glabellar lines, with results appearing in days and lasting roughly two to four months.[2] Licensed brands include Botox, Dysport, Xeomin, Jeuveau, Daxxify and Letybo, and the FDA has stated the products are not interchangeable.[2]

The only published research found on CNBTX-A is a 2008 letter in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology titled as reporting that its potency significantly exceeded labeled units in a standard potency test.[1]

angle.text: Like other botulinum toxins, it is used to relax muscles that crease the forehead and brow. Its distinguishing feature is origin and price positioning, not a different effect.

paras: CNBTX-A is a botulinum toxin A product manufactured in China, marketed under the Nanfeng name.[1] It works through the same class mechanism as other type A toxins, which relax injected muscles.

A 2008 letter in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology reported that CNBTX-A's potency significantly exceeded its labeled units in a standard potency test.[1] Because toxin units are product-specific, a labeling mismatch matters for dosing; the FDA has stated that approved brands are not interchangeable.[2]
No studies found beyond the 2008 potency letter, which tested potency rather than cosmetic outcomes.[1]

timeline.event: Letter reports CNBTX-A potency exceeding labeled units.[1]
